title: Greet the Moon
line: For Monday, the Moon’s day: reflection, rest and the tides of feeling.
intro: Selene is the Moon in Greek myth, the long-winged one who drives her chariot across the night. Monday is the Moon’s day nearly everywhere: Selene’s, Chandra’s, Tsukuyomi’s. This practice greets her with the oldest Greek hymn to the Moon.
offering: A bowl of water left under the moon, or a quiet word.

steps.title: Arrive
steps.text: Breathe like a tide: in as it rises, out as it falls back.

steps.title: Light a lamp
steps.text: A small light for the night.

steps.title: The hymn
steps.text: The opening of the Homeric Hymn to Selene. Read it aloud if you can, in Greek or in English.

steps.title: Reflect
steps.text: The Moon only reflects the Sun’s light. What light are you reflecting?
steps.prompt: What has been shining on me lately, and what have I been reflecting back?

after: The Moon waxes and wanes, and comes back. So do we.
